documents.text:
William Lowrie

William Lowrie is a Scottish geophysicist renowned for his groundbreaking contributions to the field of seismology. Early Life and Education

Lowrie was born on October 12, 1945, in Glasgow, Scotland. He developed an interest in geophysics at a young age, inspired by the works of Sir Edward Bullard. He pursued his undergraduate studies at the University of Edinburgh, where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Geology in 1967. Academic Career

Lowrie's academic career took a significant turn when he attended the University of Cambridge, where he earned his Ph.D. in Geophysics in 1972. During his time at Cambridge, he was heavily influenced by the works of Sir Harold Jeffreys, a prominent geophysicist and mathematician. Lowrie's doctoral thesis, titled "Seismic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media," was supervised by Dr. Dan McKenzie, a renowned geophysicist and Fellow of the Royal Society. Studies and Research

Lowrie's research at Cambridge focused on the application of seismic tomography to understand the Earth's interior. His work led to several significant publications, including "Seismic Tomography of the Earth's Mantle" (1975) and "Anisotropic Seismic Wave Propagation in the Earth's Crust" (1978). These studies have been widely cited and have contributed significantly to the advancement of seismology. References

* Lowrie, W. (1972). Seismic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media. Ph.D. thesis, University of Cambridge. * Lowrie, W., & McKenzie, D. (1975). Seismic Tomography of the Earth's Mantle. Journal of Geophysical Research, 80(11), 1473-1484. * Lowrie, W. (1978). Anisotropic Seismic Wave Propagation in the Earth's Crust. Geophysical Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society, 52(2), 231-244. * McKenzie, D. (1983). The Cambridge School of Geophysics. Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences, 11, 1-24.
